future_retrieval_bugs.note: Rows keep their line structure and exponents (10^19), but the PDF text layer joins cells with single spaces, so a row with an empty cell ('ByteNet [18] 23.75') no longer says which column the number belongs to. Not recoverable without glyph-level column analysis. Retrieval: keep each table in one chunk together with its caption and header rows, and have the answer step refuse to read a value off a ragged row.

Captions are their own blocks (kind=caption). Text drawn inside embedded figures is dropped on purpose (counted in fixed_in_extractor): it had figure-local coordinates and private glyph encodings ('4UBHF' for 'Stage'). Consequence: anything only stated inside a figure is not retrievable, so questions about figure contents must be refused unless the caption or body says it. Chunking must attach captions to the table/figure they describe.

Footnotes are separate blocks (kind=footnote) with the page's markers. The marker in the sentence ('Alexa^1') stays, so the sentence and its footnote (often a URL) end up in different chunks. Retrieval: low priority; markers are harmless tokens.

Every bibliography entry is its own block (kind=reference). Their titles share words with real questions ('attention', 'chunking', 'speech'), so a naive retriever returns them as evidence. Retrieval: exclude kind=reference by default. Numeric markers like [13] carry no meaning without the bibliography.

Glyphs with no Unicode mapping in the PDF font (e.g. arrows in 'tokenization�LM�detokenization'). The character is unknowable from the text layer. Harmless for retrieval of surrounding words; an answer quoting the span must not invent the symbol.

Blocks never span pages, so that every block has one page to cite. A paragraph that runs onto the next page becomes two blocks, each half a sentence at the seam. The chunker should join consecutive body blocks of the same section across a page break and cite both pages.

sub_superscripts.note: Smaller runs above/below the baseline are written ^x / _x (10^19, d_model, P_drop). Display equations still come out as linear text with ^/_ markers; that is readable for an LLM but BM25 will not match 'dmodel' against 'd_model' unless the tokenizer splits on '_' and '^' (it should).

references.note: Every bibliography entry is its own block (kind=reference). Their titles share words with real questions ('attention', 'chunking', 'speech'), so a naive retriever returns them as evidence. Retrieval: exclude kind=reference by default. Numeric markers like [13] carry no meaning without the bibliography.

kerning_splits.note: 'T ext' -> 'Text' and '6identical' -> '6 identical' are joined/split only when the papers' own vocabulary confirms the result; side-by-side runs get a space when the estimated gap is large.

accents_and_ligatures.note: TeX accents arrive as a spacing accent next to the letter ('D´ efossez'); they are recomposed to 'Défossez'.

unmapped_glyphs.note: Glyphs with no Unicode mapping in the PDF font (e.g. arrows in 'tokenization�LM�detokenization'). The character is unknowable from the text layer. Harmless for retrieval of surrounding words; an answer quoting the span must not invent the symbol.

hyphenation.note: A line-end hyphen is removed only when the joined word occurs in the papers more often than the hyphenated form ('transduc-|tion' -> 'transduction', 'sequence-|aligned' kept).

headers_footers.note: Lines in the top/bottom 8% of the page that repeat on at least 20% of pages (digits normalised), and bare page numbers there, are removed.

figure_text.note: Figure fonts with a private encoding produce text shifted by one letter ('4UBHF' = 'Stage'). Skipping embedded figures removes it; this detector checks none leaked.
